diagram_name: Anatomy of an Agent Evaluation Report
chapter_title: AI Agents, Prompts, and Rubric Scoring
learning_objective: The learner will identify the eight parts of an agent evaluation report from a description of how each looks, with at least 7 of 8 correct on the first attempt.
specification:
Type: infographic **sim-id:** agent-report-anatomy
**Library:** html
**Status:** Specified
**Bloom Level:** Remember
**Bloom Verb:** identify
**Learning Objective:** The learner will identify the eight parts of an agent evaluation report from a description of how each looks, with at least 7 of 8 correct on the first attempt. **Prerequisites:** Agent Scoring, Agent Evaluation Report, Structured Output (all defined in this chapter above this block). **Evidence of Mastery:** In quiz mode the learner clicks the marker that matches a visual hint. A click is correct when it matches the marker named in the Hint column of Content. Mastery is at least 7 of 8 correct on the first attempt. Hovering in explore mode is exploration, not evidence. **Misconceptions:** (1) A report without a not-checkable list is complete. (2) The run record is optional. (3) The recommendation replaces the evidence. **Instructional Rationale:** Identifying the parts of a report is a Remember-level task, and an illustration of one page gives each part a place. The quiz asks the learner to recognize a part by its look, which is how they will audit a real report. **Content:** The illustration is a text-free flat drawing of an evaluation report page. At the top is a wide bar with a small robot icon and a small calendar icon. Below it is a table of ten rows. Each row has a short bar for a metric name, a small numbered square, and a long bar with a small link icon. Some rows also carry a small flag icon at the right. At the bottom left is a box with three rows. At the bottom center is a wider box with a small thumbs-up icon. At the bottom right is a box with a small question-mark icon. In a thin strip along the very bottom is a small clock icon and a short tag. The eight markers: | # | Label | Hint (describes the look, not the name) | Description | Tip | |---|---|---|---|---| | 1 | Report header | The wide bar at the top with a robot icon and a calendar icon. | Names the resource, the agent, and the date of the run. | Check that the date matches the version of the resource you reviewed. | | 2 | Metric score | The small numbered square in each table row. | The whole-number score from 0 to 10 for one metric. | Count the passes in the evidence and see whether the score follows. | | 3 | Evidence | The long bar with a small link icon in each row. | The checks, results, and quotations that support the score. | Verify at least one piece of evidence in each metric yourself. | | 4 | Not-checkable flag | A small flag icon at the right of some rows. | Marks a check the agent could not verify from the text. | Follow up on every flag, and do not treat a flag as a pass. | | 5 | Totals box | The box with three rows at the bottom left. | The quality subtotal, the reusability subtotal, and the total. | Recompute the sums from the ten scores. | | 6 | Recommendation | The wider box with a thumbs-up icon at the bottom center. | The agent's adopt, revise, or reject advice, with reasons. | Apply the adoption threshold yourself before accepting it. | | 7 | Limitations | The box with a question-mark icon at the bottom right. | What the agent could not see or test, and what it assumed. | Treat each limitation as a check for a person to do. | | 8 | Run record | The thin strip with a clock icon and a short tag along the bottom. | Records the model, the date, and the prompt version. | Keep it, since a later run cannot be compared without it. | **Provenance:** The parts follow the chapter section "Agent Evaluation Report". The illustration is synthetic, and the sim labels the report "illustrative example". **Rules:** Each hint matches exactly one marker. The illustration contains no text, so every label comes from the table above. Markers are numbered 1 to 8 in the order of the table. **Learner Activity:** 1. In explore mode the learner hovers or clicks a marker and reads its label, description, and tip. 2. In quiz mode the sim shows a hint. 3. The learner clicks the marker they think the hint describes. 4. If the first click is wrong, the sim says so and lets the learner try once more. If the second click is also wrong, the sim reveals the marker and its description. 5. After all 8 hints the sim shows the summary. **Feedback:** 8 hints in a shuffled order, two attempts each. Only a correct first click counts as evidence. Correct: "Correct: [label]. [Description]". First wrong click: "Not quite. Look again at the hint: [hint]". Second wrong click: "This is [label]. [Description]". The summary shows "[n] of 8 correct on the first attempt". At 7 or more it adds "You can audit an agent's report." Below 7 it lists the labels of the missed parts. **Starting State:** The illustration with eight numbered markers, explore mode active, and the prompt "Hover a marker to see what it is." **Chapter Anchors:** The chapter says a report contains the ten scores with checks and evidence, the subtotals and band, a list of checks not verified, a recommendation, limitations, and a record of the agent, the date, and the prompt version.
